findings: I checked every word in all 16 witness files against the s24/s25 bands and fine crops. Consonants, vowels, maqaf, punctuation and order match in both languages.

Hashkivenu (HE): the split falls at וּשְׁמוֹר. It has two qamatz אָתָּה forms, a patah in the seal's אַתָּה, a final hiriq in יְרוּשָׁלָםִ, single dots after עוֹלָם and שְׁלוֹמֶךָ, and כָּל־עַמּוֹ. All match band0/band1.

Exodus 31:16–17 (HE) matches band1: בְנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵל, אֶת־הַשַּׁבָּת twice, לְדֹרֹתָם, בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל without maqaf in v.17, הִיא לְעֹלָם, כִּי־שֵׁשֶׁת, the Name printed as יְהוָה, and אֶת־הַשָּׁמַיִם וְאֶת־הָאָרֶץ. Rubric (אם שבת) and (On Sabbath) match.
Psalm 81:4–5 has בַּכֶּסֶה with segol under the kaf, as the human confirmed. Numbers 14:17 has יִגְדַּל־נָא and אֲדֹנָי. Psalm 25:6 has זְכֹר and the plene מֵעוֹלָם.

Kaddish (arc) matches band2/band3 and the crops: דִּי־בְרָא; דְכָל־בֵּית־יִשְׂרָאֵל; 'קָרִיב, וְאִמְרוּ אָמֵן.'; 'עָלְמַיָּא.'; the short spelling וְיִתְרֹמַם (holam dot only, as in next-word-vitromam); the short spelling דְּקֻדְשָׁא; doubled לְעֵלָּא וּלְעֵלָּא; מִן־כָּל־בִּרְכָתָא (final nun and two maqafs, as in next-word-mikol); 'בְּעָלְמָא, וְאִמְרוּ אָמֵן:'. The speaker label חזן is fully spelled in Rashi script (next-role-tight).

English matches s25: 'for ever,' with a comma; 'O Lord and Thy kindnesses' with no comma, as printed; 'say: Amen!' in the first Kaddish paragraph against 'say Amen!' in the third. No Hebrew catchword cues and no invented Bible citations appear. The English half-Kaddish direction appears once per book, before the opening verses, with facs n23 (HE) and n24 (EN).

Role-label scope: in HE kaddish_chatzi.xml the note חזן sits after the kaddish/yitgaddal milestone, so it falls inside that reusable part's scope. Any reuse of kaddish/yitgaddal@heidenheim (for example in another Kaddish) would carry a Reader label into a passage where it may not belong. JLPTEI-3 'Prefer milestones' says to terminate or keep part sequences clear of speaker rubrics. Birnbaum keeps its 'Reader' rubrics outside the part units (kaddish_chatzi, arvit_hashkivenu, shabbat_arvit_hashkivenu_text). The label should come before the milestone, still at the head of the same

.

The two rubrics are typed correctly against the 'Kinds of rubric' rules and the ODD. (אם שבת)/(On Sabbath) is the conditional's own instruction note; the ODD allows one optional note before the condition, and it is an instruction. 'The Reader says half Kaddish.' and חזן are descriptions placed inside the governed content. xml:lang is correct: arc paragraphs, a he note, and en descriptions in the HE book.

Every feature used is in features.yaml with the right kind: holiday-aggregate/aseret-ymei-tshuva, holiday-aggregate/shabbat, quorum/minyan, service-time/*, holiday/rosh-hashana (numeric), hebrew-date month/day. aseret-ymei-tshuva is 'derived', which the registry allows a volume to declare.

Each Bible file is exact. Its verse milestones carry canonical corresp, followed by a bare verse terminator and a bare chapter terminator, with no chapter-level corresp and no whole-chapter claim. Publication URNs use the edition-qualified absolute range form (exodus/31/16-/31/17, psalms/81/4-/81/5) or single verses. Every file has biblScope 15–15.

Not blocking: the opening <milestone unit='chapter' n='…'/> has no corresp. By rule 3 that makes it a terminator that opens nothing, so it is not a 'canonical chapter milestone' as the brief says. It is harmless, and it matches the existing deuteronomy pattern as I understand it, but the markup carries no chapter identity.
Not blocking: EN header titles lack spaces ('Exodus31:16–17', 'Psalm81:4–5', 'Numbers14:17', 'Psalm25:6').

No new canonical identity: kaddish/chatzi, kaddish/{yitgaddal,yehe_shemeh,yitbarakh}, hashkivenu/opening, hashkivenu/hapores_sukkat_shalom(/text) and siddur:shabbat/arvit/verses/veshamru are all existing names. The first five are confirmed in the Birnbaum files I opened. I did not open a file defining veshamru (see limits). No text corresp repeats within a document.

HE and EN share the same milestone corresps: hashkivenu/opening; hapores_sukkat_shalom/text; exodus/31/16 and 17; psalms/81/4 and 5; numbers/14/17; psalms/25/6; kaddish/yitgaddal, yehe_shemeh, yitbarakh. Each sequence ends with a terminator, and the root divs (prayer:hashkivenu, …/hapores_sukkat_shalom, kaddish/chatzi) match.

The Hashkivenu split matches Birnbaum. Birnbaum hashkivenu/opening ends at אָתָּה before its weekday seal. Birnbaum's hapores_sukkat_shalom/text starts at וּשְׁמוֹר. The maḥzor opening likewise ends at 'merciful King.' / וְרַחוּם אָתָּה.

Psalm 81 in English splits v.4/v.5 at 'festival, / for it is…', which is a reasonable verse boundary inside one English sentence. The page-15 module boundaries split one printed paragraph (Hashkivenu); no printed paragraph break has been invented.

The documentary books carry the Veshamru URN on a div that wraps the conditional and the transclusion, in both HE and EN, so the two books pair at that level. The expanded book's Veshamru div does not carry the URN. Nothing breaks, but the brief's statement that Veshamru reuses the URN holds only for the two documentary books.

The first-night Maariv order is: emet_veemunah → hashkivenu → [Shabbat gate, with the source's HE and EN rubrics: Exodus 31:16–17] → Psalm 81:4–5 → [minyan gate: one English description → Numbers 14:17 → Psalm 25:6 → kaddish/chatzi]. This is the order of the source and of both documentary books. The direction is printed once, before the opening verses. חזן comes in through the Kaddish file. There is no second Hebrew direction.
The Veshamru gate tests holiday-aggregate/shabbat and declares the same value inside it. The pure Bible verse files carry no Shabbat condition of their own, which is correct.

Not blocking: the Maariv minyan gate, like Barekhu, has no rubric. The Minchah gates on Half Kaddish, the Reader's repetition and Whole Kaddish carry the editorial 'במניין: / With a minyan:'. When minyan is undecided, the Maariv passage is set off only by the English description it opens with. Consider making the gates consistent; this is editorial and does not affect source fidelity.

Correction to the brief: only machzor_expanded declares aseret-ymei-tshuva=true locally in first-night Maariv (section_first_night_maariv_settings, inside the rosh-hashana=1 and maariv gate). The two documentary indexes declare nothing. Their HE and EN Kaddish conditionals therefore depend on the volume's settings. Per JLPTEI-3: with no date the condition is undecided and the Kaddish is kept without delimiters, which is faithful. A dated build or reader's device outside the Ten Days would leave out the unconditionally printed page-15 Kaddish in both languages. Adding a local j:declare is not a clean fix, because a declaration of the kind of day is itself treated as a condition, judged against the day (JLPTEI-3 'Conditions on a running order'). Please confirm the documentary settings files and electronic-book behaviour are intended.

Elul 29 Minchah is correctly isolated. It requires and declares shabbat=false, yom-tov=false, aseret=false and 6/29, and binds kaddish/chatzi and kaddish/shalem explicitly to Birnbaum. Erev Rosh Hashanah can never be Shabbat, so shabbat=false always holds. With aseret=false in scope, both maḥzor Kaddish files (HE and EN, each gated aseret=true) are false. The festival English is suppressed, not imported as a translation that is absent here.

Birnbaum kaddish_chatzi.xml and kaddish_yatom.xml now bind their yitgaddal, yehe_shemeh and yitbarakh children to @hasiddur_hashalem-birnbaum-1949-he, so maḥzor parts sharing those names cannot substitute into a Birnbaum Kaddish. Verified.

Risk: the gate suppresses; it does not fall back. Any book whose project priority puts the maḥzor ahead of Birnbaum and transcludes an unqualified kaddish/chatzi outside the Ten Days would get the maḥzor file, whose condition is false, and would lose the Half Kaddish rather than fall back to Birnbaum. The reverse also applies: expanded Maariv uses unqualified kaddish/chatzi and hashkivenu. If Birnbaum outranks the maḥzor there, the result is ordinary-day Kaddish wording and Birnbaum's weekday seal שומר עמו ישראל לעד on Rosh Hashanah night. The Minchah sections avoid this by binding explicitly. Consider binding the Maariv Kaddish (and Hashkivenu) to @prayerbook_for_the_new_year-heidenheim-1965-he, or confirm the priority settings.

Kabbalat Shabbat is not really 'ordinary'. In this volume it is reached only when Rosh Hashanah falls on Shabbat, which is 1 Tishrei and inside the Ten Days. Its Mourner's Kaddish (unqualified kaddish/yatom, which resolves to Birnbaum with self-bound children) will print Birnbaum's wording, and its yitbarakh and oseh shalom may be the ordinary-day forms. The maḥzor prints only the direction קדיש יתום there, so nothing should be invented. Still, a Ten Days calendar context is being fed an ordinary-day dependency, and that should be decided on purpose. This belongs to the earlier installment; it is not a change required here.
Morning Shacharit declares service-time and rosh-hashana=1. Its context stays separate from first-night Maariv, which declares maariv=true and switches off the other service times.
